## Context

Twyne already has most of the parts of a "fluid" editor, but each decides on its own when to appear:
- the struggle tracker opens one margin tool when a paragraph looks stuck (`extensions/struggle-tracker.ts`)
- background research files sources (`utils/background-research.ts`)
- comments and persona notes sit in the Editorial Board side panel
- zen mode is manual only (the `twyne:zen-mode` event)

The writer still has to open panels to see things. The goal is that everything reaches the writer in the flow of writing, with nothing opened by hand:
- The app reads whether you are **in flow, working, or stuck**. Jev confirms the borderline cases.
- It goes quiet in flow and fades into zen mode on its own.
- When you're stuck, it brings forward the single most useful item:
  - a comment or persona reply as it streams in
  - a source
  - a book or album card with its cover
  - a passage from your other work
  - a charter standard you're breaking
- Hovering a comment draws arrows to the passages and cards it connects to.
- It learns your rhythms and which kinds of help you actually use.

Second request, same underlying need: the data model has no clear hierarchy or language.
- Dossiers and briefs are the same thing under two names.
- There's no grouping above a single folio.
- There are no standards that follow you across pieces.
- The dossier is fixed once filed, even though intent changes as you write.

User decisions:
- **Names:** French editorial house language.
- **Sync:** collections, charters and the ledger go into Convex tables now.
- **Cover lookups:** on by default, with a switch.

## The language (goes into UI copy, docs, and code names)

| Term | What it is |
|---|---|
| **House** | The writer. Holds the house charter and default dossier fields. One per account. |
| **Collection** | A series of folios, like a publisher's *collection* (Série noire). Holds a shared dossier layer and a collection charter. |
| **Folio** | One piece of writing. Unchanged. |
| **Dossier** | What a piece is for: audience, goal, tone, constraints, references. The internal type stays `ProjectBrief`; "brief" is retired from UI copy. |
| **Charter** | Standards and requirements. Each item is a short rule with a severity (*must* or *prefer*) and a scope. Charters stack from House to Collection to Folio. |
| **Edition** | A filed version of a dossier. Already exists (`utils/brief-history.ts`). |
| **Revision** | A version of the manuscript text. Already exists (Lix). |
| **Amendment** | A change to the dossier that the draft proposes ("your pages now read for practitioners"). The writer files it, amends it, or sets it aside. Filing one creates an Edition. |
| **Context stack** | House, then Collection, then Folio dossier, then filed amendments, then the current moment. This is exactly what the models receive. |
| **Ledger** | An append-only log of every context change: who or what made it, when, and why. |

A revision changes the words. An edition changes what the words are for.

## Part A — the flow layer

### New pure modules (unit-tested, no DOM)

- **`src/utils/flow-state.ts`** reads flow from typing cadence.
  - Input: keystroke samples (time, inserted, deleted), pointer and panel activity, and the struggle score from `readStruggle` (`utils/struggle-signals.ts`).
  - Output: `flow | working | stuck | away`.
  - Hysteresis: entering flow needs sustained steady typing (a minimum active ratio and a low delete ratio over a window). Leaving flow needs a real pause, a move to the margin or masthead, or Escape.
  - An intermediate `settling` stage dims the chrome before full zen.
  - Thresholds come from the profile, not constants.
- **`src/utils/flow-profile.ts`** learns the writer's patterns.
  - Rolling samples of burst length, pause length, and the time it takes to reach flow.
  - Hour-of-day writing histogram.
  - Per item-kind engagement counts: `shown`, `engaged`, `dismissed`, `ignored`.
  - Derives `stuckPauseMs`, `flowEntryMs`, `exitPauseMs`, and `kindWeight(kind)`. The weight is Laplace-smoothed, so it starts neutral.
  - Pure update functions, plus load and save through `loadMetaFromIdb`/`saveMetaToIdb` (`utils/idb.ts`).
- **`src/utils/flow-items.ts`** defines the item model and the surfacing policy.
  - `FlowItem` kinds: `tool | comment | persona-note | source | work (book/album/song/film) | shelf (dossier attachment / bibliography match) | echo (your other work) | charter | amendment`.
  - Every item has anchor quotes, a priority, a timestamp, and optional `links` to other items and passages.
  - `decideSurface(state, items, profile, cursor)` returns visible items, held items, and a reason for each:
    - **flow:** nothing new appears; items are held.
    - **working:** at most two cards near the viewport, plus ticks.
    - **stuck:** the single best item for the cursor's paragraph, plus its links.
  - Scoring: kind weight × proximity to the cursor paragraph × freshness × Jev relevance.
  - Also exports `stackCards(desiredTops, heights, obstacles)` to avoid collisions in the margin.
- **`src/utils/flow-connections.ts`** finds connections locally.
  - Tokenizes and builds a small TF-IDF index over paragraphs from other folios (`loadFoliosFromIdb`, `loadFolioContentFromIdb`, `htmlToPlainText` from `utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`) and over the current manuscript.
  - `relatedPassages(text, index, k)` returns candidates that Jev then confirms.
  - `workCandidates(paragraph, marks)` pulls quoted or italic titles and research targets of kind `work` (`utils/research-targets.ts`).
  - Also matches the paragraph against dossier attachments and bibliography entries (`utils/bibliography.ts`) for shelf items.
- **`src/utils/flow-media.ts`** fetches covers.
  - Books: OpenLibrary `search.json`, then `covers.openlibrary.org`.
  - Albums and songs: MusicBrainz `ws/2/release-group` and `recording`, then `coverartarchive.org`.
  - Only the title Jev picked is sent.
  - Throttled to 1 request per second (MusicBrainz's limit), cached in IDB meta, and returns nothing when the switch is off.
  - Cards show the title, creator, cover and a link, never lyric text.
- **`src/utils/flow-diagnostics.ts`** keeps a ring buffer of the last 300 decisions and persists it to IDB meta, throttled.
  - Each entry records: state transition and its signals, Jev request and answer, latency and budget, items surfaced or held with reasons, and the context-stack hash used.
  - Emits `twyne:flow-diagnostics`.

### Runtime

- **`src/components/editor/extensions/flow-conductor.ts`** follows the lifecycle of `startInFlowTools`. It is started next to it in `twyne-editor.tsx` (around line 861), with the same `getClient`, `folioId` and brief.
  - It feeds transactions and pointer events to `flow-state`.
  - It asks Jev only at the edges, through `askJudgement` (`utils/judgement-client.ts`) and the shared budget in `utils/system-one-budget.ts`, batching several questions per request:
    - "Is the writer in sustained composition, so interruptions should be withheld?" (noul)
    - "Is the writer stuck?"
    - "Does this candidate bear on the current paragraph?"
    - "What kind of work is this title: book, album, song, film, or none?"
    - "Is a charter standard breached here?"
  - When Jev is unavailable, the local heuristics decide on their own.
  - It gathers items from existing events without changing their producers:
    - `IN_FLOW_EVENT`: the active tool
    - `twyne:user-comments-changed` plus `loadUserComments` (`utils/user-comments.ts`)
    - `twyne:persona-notes`
    - `twyne:persona-reply-stream` and `twyne:persona-reply`: streaming text updates the card live
    - `twyne:background-sources`, then a bibliography lookup
  - Auto-zen dispatches `twyne:zen-mode` with `{on, source: "flow"}`. A manual toggle, with no source, sets a manual override that is respected for 10 minutes and recorded in the profile.
  - It sets `document.documentElement.dataset.flow` so CSS can fade the chrome gradually.
  - It publishes a snapshot on `twyne:flow`.
- **`src/components/in-flow/flow-surface.tsx`** is mounted beside `<MarginRails>` in `manuscript-panel.tsx:159`.
  - **Right margin:** the room (comments, persona replies as they stream, sources, works, charter and amendment cards).
  - **Left margin:** your own work (echoes and shelf matches), placed below the existing "Your tools" shelf.
  - Cards are stacked with `stackCards`, avoiding the in-flow tool card's rect.
  - Hovering a card, or a `.twyne-comment-mark` / `.twyne-persona-note` in the text, draws an SVG overlay of arrows to every linked passage and card. Passage ranges are found with the existing `findTextRange` logic, which moves into a shared util.
  - When a margin is too narrow, cards fall back to a single dock at the bottom of the viewport, mirroring the `mode: "popover"` behaviour in `margin-rail.tsx`.
  - Dismissing or engaging a card feeds the profile.
  - Everything is hidden in zen mode and in print.
- **Wiring changes**
  - `twyne-editor.tsx`: start the conductor; listen for `twyne:zen-mode` events with `source: "flow"` and set `store.zenMode`.
  - `review-controls.tsx`: add two switches next to "Margin tools": "Read my flow (automatic focus)" and "Cover lookups".
  - `global.css`: append flow-surface, arrow and `[data-flow]` fade rules in the existing `.in-flow-*` style.

## Part B — the House context model

(Convex details are filled in below from the data-model survey.)

### Model and storage
- **`src/utils/context-stack.ts`**
  - Types: `House`, `Collection { id, name, folioIds, dossier: Partial<ProjectInterviewAnswers>, attachments, charterId }`, `Charter { id, scope: house|collection|folio, ownerId, items: CharterItem[] }`, `CharterItem { id, text, severity: must|prefer, kind?: length|citation|style|voice|other }`, `LedgerEntry { at, layer, field, from, to, source: interview|refine|amendment|collection|manual, reason }`.
  - `assembleContextStack(folioId)` merges the layers. A field is inherited from Collection and House when the folio leaves it blank, and each field is tagged with the layer it came from.
  - `contextForModels(stack)` returns the compact string plus a token estimate for each layer.
  - `effectiveBrief(stack)` returns a `ProjectBrief`, so existing read-only consumers can use the merged view.
- **Local first:** records live in IDB meta under `house`, `house-collections`, `charters` and `context-ledger`.
  - Every write goes through `toStorable` (`utils/idb.ts:445`) and is read back to verify it.
  - This avoids the known silent failure where a Qwik proxy causes a `DataCloneError` on an IDB write.
- **Convex tables** (read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` first).
  - Named to avoid confusion with the generic row-storage helper `convex/lib/collections.ts`.
  - Lists are rows, not arrays, per the guidelines.
  - Tables:
    - `houses`: userId, dossierDefaults, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`
    - `houseCollections`: userId, collectionId, name, dossier, charterNote, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`, `by_userId_and_collectionId`
    - `collectionMembers`: userId, collectionId, folioId; indexed `by_userId_and_collectionId`, `by_userId_and_folioId`
    - `charterItems`: userId, itemId, scope, ownerRef, text, severity, kind, order, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`, `by_userId_and_ownerRef`
    - `contextLedger`: userId, entryId, at, layer, ownerRef, field, from, to, source, reason; indexed `by_userId_and_at`, paginated
- **`convex/house.ts`** follows the auth pattern in `convex/userComments.ts`.
  - The owner is always `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity().tokenIdentifier`, never passed in as an argument.
  - Functions: `getHouse` (the whole house: collections, members, charter items); `upsertHouse`, `upsertCollection`, `deleteCollection`, `setCollectionMembers`, `upsertCharterItem`, `deleteCharterItem`; `appendLedgerEntries` (idempotent on `entryId`); `listLedger` (paginated).
- **`src/utils/house-sync.ts`** pushes each change while signed in and pulls on load and sign-in. The pull hook goes next to the existing dossier pull in `convex-sync.ts`.
- **Tests:** `convex/house.test.ts` in the `describeConvex` style of `convex/userComments.test.ts`, including a second identity that must not see the first writer's rows.
- **Edition provenance:** `archiveBriefEdition` gains an optional `source` and `reason`, and writes a ledger entry.

### Fluid dossier (amendments)
- **`src/utils/context-drift.ts`** (pure plus a runner) asks Jev every N new words, and only outside flow: "Does the recent writing still serve the dossier's stated goal / audience / tone?"
  - Two low readings in a row produce an `amendment` FlowItem.
  - The proposed wording comes from the writer's model (a single-shot helper in `ai-client.ts`). With no model configured, the card asks the writer to type it.
  - Filing uses `saveProjectBriefForFolio` (`utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`), which already archives an Edition, and adds a ledger entry with `source: "amendment"`.
- **Charter enforcement:** on a pause while *working*, the conductor asks Jev per applicable charter item (batched, *must* items first). A breach becomes a `charter` card anchored to the paragraph. This is how standards follow the writer across pieces.

### Inspection and visuals
- **`/context` route** (`src/routes/context/index.tsx`), in the Library's typewriter style (`dept-label`, `--font-typewriter`, `--font-display`, `btn-paper`). Tabs:
  1. **The House:** the hierarchy diagram. Click a level to edit it: house charter, collections (create, add folios), collection dossier and charter.
  2. **Context stack:** the active folio's merged stack. Each field is stamped with its source layer, and the exact text the models get is shown.
  3. **Ledger and editions:** a timeline of every context change and dossier edition. Amendments appear as stamped "AVENANT" slips.
  4. **Diagnostics** (developers; shown when `import.meta.env.DEV` or `?diagnostics=1`): conductor decisions, Jev calls with latency and answers, budget state, per-layer token estimates, flow-profile numbers, and a JSON export.
- **`src/components/context/house-diagram.tsx`** is an inline SVG in the mid-century French editorial style:
  - a letterhead for the House
  - index-card drawers for Collections
  - manila folders for Folios, with a clipped dossier sheet and a stamped charter
  - carbon-copy stacks for Editions and Revisions
  - It works in both themes with the existing color tokens. A compact version appears in the Library header.
- Links to `/context`: the Library, the dossier refine page, and the editor's folio menu.
- **`docs/flow-and-context.md`** holds the glossary and the architecture.

## Build order (each phase ships working and tested)
1. Pure flow modules (`flow-state`, `flow-profile`, `flow-items`) with tests; the conductor with auto-zen, the chrome fade and the manual override; the settings switches.
2. `flow-surface`: comment, persona-note and source cards, streaming replies, hover arrows, dismiss and engagement learning.
3. Connections and media: echoes from other folios, shelf matches, book and album cards.
4. The context model: `context-stack`, Convex tables and `house.ts`, `house-sync`, edition provenance, the ledger.
5. The fluid dossier: drift readings, amendment cards, charter enforcement cards.
6. The `/context` inspector, the house diagram, the diagnostics tab, the glossary doc, and links in.

Working-tree caution: `twyne-editor.tsx`, `manuscript-panel.tsx`, `routes/editor/index.tsx`, `global.css`, `convex/schema.ts` and `convex/sync.ts` already have uncommitted changes from other work. Edits there stay small and additive (CSS is appended at the end), and no unrelated line is touched.

## Verification
- Unit tests (bun, run file by file; the full suite has known cross-file flakes): `flow-state`, `flow-profile`, `flow-items` (surfacing and stacking), `flow-connections`, `flow-media` (mocked fetch, switch off means no requests), `context-stack` (merge and provenance), `context-drift`. Use `convex-test` for the new Convex functions, including auth refusal.
- `bun run build.types` and `bun run lint`.
- Playwright e2e (`e2e/flow-surface.e2e.ts`):
  - steady typing adds `data-flow="flow"` and turns on zen
  - a pause brings the chrome back
  - a seeded comment shows as a margin card, and hovering it draws arrows
  - `/context` renders the diagram, the stack and the diagnostics
- Manual check in the browser via `bun run dev.frontend` and Claude in Chrome: record a GIF of entering flow, a stuck pause surfacing a card, hover arrows, and filing an amendment.

# Fluid editor + the House context model

## Context

Twyne already has most of the parts of a "fluid" editor, but each decides on its own when to appear:
- the struggle tracker opens one margin tool when a paragraph looks stuck (`extensions/struggle-tracker.ts`)
- background research files sources (`utils/background-research.ts`)
- comments and persona notes sit in the Editorial Board side panel
- zen mode is manual only (the `twyne:zen-mode` event)

The writer still has to open panels to see things. The goal is that everything reaches the writer in the flow of writing, with nothing opened by hand:
- The app reads whether you are **in flow, working, or stuck**. Jev confirms the borderline cases.
- It goes quiet in flow and fades into zen mode on its own.
- When you're stuck, it brings forward the single most useful item:
  - a comment or persona reply as it streams in
  - a source
  - a book or album card with its cover
  - a passage from your other work
  - a charter standard you're breaking
- Hovering a comment draws arrows to the passages and cards it connects to.
- It learns your rhythms and which kinds of help you actually use.

Second request, same underlying need: the data model has no clear hierarchy or language.
- Dossiers and briefs are the same thing under two names.
- There's no grouping above a single folio.
- There are no standards that follow you across pieces.
- The dossier is fixed once filed, even though intent changes as you write.

User decisions:
- **Names:** French editorial house language.
- **Sync:** collections, charters and the ledger go into Convex tables now.
- **Cover lookups:** on by default, with a switch.

## The language (goes into UI copy, docs, and code names)

| Term | What it is |
|---|---|
| **House** | The writer. Holds the house charter and default dossier fields. One per account. |
| **Collection** | A series of folios, like a publisher's *collection* (Série noire). Holds a shared dossier layer and a collection charter. |
| **Folio** | One piece of writing. Unchanged. |
| **Dossier** | What a piece is for: audience, goal, tone, constraints, references. The internal type stays `ProjectBrief`; "brief" is retired from UI copy. |
| **Charter** | Standards and requirements. Each item is a short rule with a severity (*must* or *prefer*) and a scope. Charters stack from House to Collection to Folio. |
| **Edition** | A filed version of a dossier. Already exists (`utils/brief-history.ts`). |
| **Revision** | A version of the manuscript text. Already exists (Lix). |
| **Amendment** | A change to the dossier that the draft proposes ("your pages now read for practitioners"). The writer files it, amends it, or sets it aside. Filing one creates an Edition. |
| **Context stack** | House, then Collection, then Folio dossier, then filed amendments, then the current moment. This is exactly what the models receive. |
| **Ledger** | An append-only log of every context change: who or what made it, when, and why. |

A revision changes the words. An edition changes what the words are for.

## Part A — the flow layer

### New pure modules (unit-tested, no DOM)

- **`src/utils/flow-state.ts`** reads flow from typing cadence.
  - Input: keystroke samples (time, inserted, deleted), pointer and panel activity, and the struggle score from `readStruggle` (`utils/struggle-signals.ts`).
  - Output: `flow | working | stuck | away`.
  - Hysteresis: entering flow needs sustained steady typing (a minimum active ratio and a low delete ratio over a window). Leaving flow needs a real pause, a move to the margin or masthead, or Escape.
  - An intermediate `settling` stage dims the chrome before full zen.
  - Thresholds come from the profile, not constants.
- **`src/utils/flow-profile.ts`** learns the writer's patterns.
  - Rolling samples of burst length, pause length, and the time it takes to reach flow.
  - Hour-of-day writing histogram.
  - Per item-kind engagement counts: `shown`, `engaged`, `dismissed`, `ignored`.
  - Derives `stuckPauseMs`, `flowEntryMs`, `exitPauseMs`, and `kindWeight(kind)`. The weight is Laplace-smoothed, so it starts neutral.
  - Pure update functions, plus load and save through `loadMetaFromIdb`/`saveMetaToIdb` (`utils/idb.ts`).
- **`src/utils/flow-items.ts`** defines the item model and the surfacing policy.
  - `FlowItem` kinds: `tool | comment | persona-note | source | work (book/album/song/film) | shelf (dossier attachment / bibliography match) | echo (your other work) | charter | amendment`.
  - Every item has anchor quotes, a priority, a timestamp, and optional `links` to other items and passages.
  - `decideSurface(state, items, profile, cursor)` returns visible items, held items, and a reason for each:
    - **flow:** nothing new appears; items are held.
    - **working:** at most two cards near the viewport, plus ticks.
    - **stuck:** the single best item for the cursor's paragraph, plus its links.
  - Scoring: kind weight × proximity to the cursor paragraph × freshness × Jev relevance.
  - Also exports `stackCards(desiredTops, heights, obstacles)` to avoid collisions in the margin.
- **`src/utils/flow-connections.ts`** finds connections locally.
  - Tokenizes and builds a small TF-IDF index over paragraphs from other folios (`loadFoliosFromIdb`, `loadFolioContentFromIdb`, `htmlToPlainText` from `utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`) and over the current manuscript.
  - `relatedPassages(text, index, k)` returns candidates that Jev then confirms.

  - Emits `twyne:flow-diagnostics`.

- **`src/components/editor/extensions/flow-conductor.ts`** follows the lifecycle of `startInFlowTools`. It is started next to it in `twyne-editor.tsx` (around line 861), with the same `getClient`, `folioId` and brief.

    - "Is the writer stuck?"
    - "Does this candidate bear on the current paragraph?"
    - "What kind of work is this title: book, album, song, film, or none?"
    - "Is a charter standard breached here?"
  - When Jev is unavailable, the local heuristics decide on their own.

    - `twyne:persona-notes`
    - `twyne:persona-reply-stream` and `twyne:persona-reply`: streaming text updates the card live
    - `twyne:background-sources`, then a bibliography lookup
  - Auto-zen dispatches `twyne:zen-mode` with `{on, source: "flow"}`. A manual toggle, with no source, sets a manual override that is respected for 10 minutes and recorded in the profile.
  - It sets `document.documentElement.dataset.flow` so CSS can fade the chrome gradually.
  - It publishes a snapshot on `twyne:flow`.

  - **Left margin:** your own work (echoes and shelf matches), placed below the existing "Your tools" shelf.

  - Dismissing or engaging a card feeds the profile.
  - Everything is hidden in zen mode and in print.

{"index":2,"status":"fulfilled","value":{"chunk_id":"ecb09b","wall_time_seconds":0.000019183,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4159,"output":"# Fluid editor + the House context model

## Context

Twyne already has most of the parts of a "fluid" editor, but each decides on its own when to appear:
- the struggle tracker opens one margin tool when a paragraph looks stuck (`extensions/struggle-tracker.ts`)
- background research files sources (`utils/background-research.ts`)
- comments and persona notes sit in the Editorial Board side panel
- zen mode is manual only (the `twyne:zen-mode` event)

The writer still has to open panels to see things. The goal is that everything reaches the writer in the flow of writing, with nothing opened by hand:
- The app reads whether you are **in flow, working, or stuck**. Jev confirms the borderline cases.
- It goes quiet in flow and fades into zen mode on its own.
- When you're stuck, it brings forward the single most useful item:
  - a comment or persona reply as it streams in
  - a source
  - a book or album card with its cover
  - a passage from your other work
  - a charter standard you're breaking
- Hovering a comment draws arrows to the passages and cards it connects to.
- It learns your rhythms and which kinds of help you actually use.

Second request, same underlying need: the data model has no clear hierarchy or language.
- Dossiers and briefs are the same thing under two names.
- There's no grouping above a single folio.
- There are no standards that follow you across pieces.
- The dossier is fixed once filed, even though intent changes as you write.

User decisions:
- **Names:** French editorial house language.
- **Sync:** collections, charters and the ledger go into Convex tables now.
- **Cover lookups:** on by default, with a switch.

## The language (goes into UI copy, docs, and code names)

| Term | What it is |
|---|---|
| **House** | The writer. Holds the house charter and default dossier fields. One per account. |
| **Collection** | A series of folios, like a publisher's *collection* (Série noire). Holds a shared dossier layer and a collection charter. |
| **Folio** | One piece of writing. Unchanged. |
| **Dossier** | What a piece is for: audience, goal, tone, constraints, references. The internal type stays `ProjectBrief`; "brief" is retired from UI copy. |
| **Charter** | Standards and requirements. Each item is a short rule with a severity (*must* or *prefer*) and a scope. Charters stack from House to Collection to Folio. |
| **Edition** | A filed version of a dossier. Already exists (`utils/brief-history.ts`). |
| **Revision** | A version of the manuscript text. Already exists (Lix). |
| **Amendment** | A change to the dossier that the draft proposes ("your pages now read for practitioners"). The writer files it, amends it, or sets it aside. Filing one creates an Edition. |
| **Context stack** | House, then Collection, then Folio dossier, then filed amendments, then the current moment. This is exactly what the models receive. |
| **Ledger** | An append-only log of every context change: who or what made it, when, and why. |

A revision changes the words. An edition changes what the words are for.

## Part A — the flow layer

### New pure modules (unit-tested, no DOM)

- **`src/utils/flow-state.ts`** reads flow from typing cadence.
  - Input: keystroke samples (time, inserted, deleted), pointer and panel activity, and the struggle score from `readStruggle` (`utils/struggle-signals.ts`).
  - Output: `flow | working | stuck | away`.
  - Hysteresis: entering flow needs sustained steady typing (a minimum active ratio and a low delete ratio over a window). Leaving flow needs a real pause, a move to the margin or masthead, or Escape.
  - An intermediate `settling` stage dims the chrome before full zen.
  - Thresholds come from the profile, not constants.
- **`src/utils/flow-profile.ts`** learns the writer's patterns.
  - Rolling samples of burst length, pause length, and the time it takes to reach flow.
  - Hour-of-day writing histogram.
  - Per item-kind engagement counts: `shown`, `engaged`, `dismissed`, `ignored`.
  - Derives `stuckPauseMs`, `flowEntryMs`, `exitPauseMs`, and `kindWeight(kind)`. The weight is Laplace-smoothed, so it starts neutral.
  - Pure update functions, plus load and save through `loadMetaFromIdb`/`saveMetaToIdb` (`utils/idb.ts`).
- **`src/utils/flow-items.ts`** defines the item model and the surfacing policy.
  - `FlowItem` kinds: `tool | comment | persona-note | source | work (book/album/song/film) | shelf (dossier attachment / bibliography match) | echo (your other work) | charter | amendment`.
  - Every item has anchor quotes, a priority, a timestamp, and optional `links` to other items and passages.
  - `decideSurface(state, items, profile, cursor)` returns visible items, held items, and a reason for each:
    - **flow:** nothing new appears; items are held.
    - **working:** at most two cards near the viewport, plus ticks.
    - **stuck:** the single best item for the cursor's paragraph, plus its links.
  - Scoring: kind weight × proximity to the cursor paragraph × freshness × Jev relevance.
  - Also exports `stackCards(desiredTops, heights, obstacles)` to avoid collisions in the margin.
- **`src/utils/flow-connections.ts`** finds connections locally.
  - Tokenizes and builds a small TF-IDF index over paragraphs from other folios (`loadFoliosFromIdb`, `loadFolioContentFromIdb`, `htmlToPlainText` from `utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`) and over the current manuscript.
  - `relatedPassages(text, index, k)` returns candidates that Jev then confirms.
  - `workCandidates(paragraph, marks)` pulls quoted or italic titles and research targets of kind `work` (`utils/research-targets.ts`).
  - Also matches the paragraph against dossier attachments and bibliography entries (`utils/bibliography.ts`) for shelf items.
- **`src/utils/flow-media.ts`** fetches covers.
  - Books: OpenLibrary `search.json`, then `covers.openlibrary.org`.
  - Albums and songs: MusicBrainz `ws/2/release-group` and `recording`, then `coverartarchive.org`.
  - Only the title Jev picked is sent.
  - Throttled to 1 request per second (MusicBrainz's limit), cached in IDB meta, and returns nothing when the switch is off.
  - Cards show the title, creator, cover and a link, never lyric text.
- **`src/utils/flow-diagnostics.ts`** keeps a ring buffer of the last 300 decisions and persists it to IDB meta, throttled.
  - Each entry records: state transition and its signals, Jev request and answer, latency and budget, items surfaced or held with reasons, and the context-stack hash used.
  - Emits `twyne:flow-diagnostics`.

### Runtime

- **`src/components/editor/extensions/flow-conductor.ts`** follows the lifecycle of `startInFlowTools`. It is started next to it in `twyne-editor.tsx` (around line 861), with the same `getClient`, `folioId` and brief.
  - It feeds transactions and pointer events to `flow-state`.
  - It asks Jev only at the edges, through `askJudgement` (`utils/judgement-client.ts`) and the shared budget in `utils/system-one-budget.ts`, batching several questions per request:
    - "Is the writer in sustained composition, so interruptions should be withheld?" (noul)
    - "Is the writer stuck?"
    - "Does this candidate bear on the current paragraph?"
    - "What kind of work is this title: book, album, song, film, or none?"
    - "Is a charter standard breached here?"
  - When Jev is unavailable, the local heuristics decide on their own.
  - It gathers items from existing events without changing their producers:
    - `IN_FLOW_EVENT`: the active tool
    - `twyne:user-comments-changed` plus `loadUserComments` (`utils/user-comments.ts`)
    - `twyne:persona-notes`
    - `twyne:persona-reply-stream` and `twyne:persona-reply`: streaming text updates the card live
    - `twyne:background-sources`, then a bibliography lookup
  - Auto-zen dispatches `twyne:zen-mode` with `{on, source: "flow"}`. A manual toggle, with no source, sets a manual override that is respected for 10 minutes and recorded in the profile.
  - It sets `document.documentElement.dataset.flow` so CSS can fade the chrome gradually.
  - It publishes a snapshot on `twyne:flow`.
- **`src/components/in-flow/flow-surface.tsx`** is mounted beside `<MarginRails>` in `manuscript-panel.tsx:159`.
  - **Right margin:** the room (comments, persona replies as they stream, sources, works, charter and amendment cards).
  - **Left margin:** your own work (echoes and shelf matches), placed below the existing "Your tools" shelf.
  - Cards are stacked with `stackCards`, avoiding the in-flow tool card's rect.
  - Hovering a card, or a `.twyne-comment-mark` / `.twyne-persona-note` in the text, draws an SVG overlay of arrows to every linked passage and card. Passage ranges are found with the existing `findTextRange` logic, which moves into a shared util.
  - When a margin is too …342 tokens truncated…tagged with the layer it came from.
  - `contextForModels(stack)` returns the compact string plus a token estimate for each layer.
  - `effectiveBrief(stack)` returns a `ProjectBrief`, so existing read-only consumers can use the merged view.
- **Local first:** records live in IDB meta under `house`, `house-collections`, `charters` and `context-ledger`.
  - Every write goes through `toStorable` (`utils/idb.ts:445`) and is read back to verify it.
  - This avoids the known silent failure where a Qwik proxy causes a `DataCloneError` on an IDB write.
- **Convex tables** (read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` first).
  - Named to avoid confusion with the generic row-storage helper `convex/lib/collections.ts`.
  - Lists are rows, not arrays, per the guidelines.
  - Tables:
    - `houses`: userId, dossierDefaults, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`
    - `houseCollections`: userId, collectionId, name, dossier, charterNote, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`, `by_userId_and_collectionId`
    - `collectionMembers`: userId, collectionId, folioId; indexed `by_userId_and_collectionId`, `by_userId_and_folioId`
    - `charterItems`: userId, itemId, scope, ownerRef, text, severity, kind, order, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`, `by_userId_and_ownerRef`

### Galley slips

Entering `flow` opens a session. Leaving for any other reading closes it; Escape,
reaching for the room, turning focus off, disabling automatic focus, destroying
the editor or changing folios closes it too. A session worth remembering lasts
at least one minute **or** adds forty net words. Shorter runs leave no slip.

The slip records its folio, start and end, time in flow, net document word growth
(never negative), rounded words per minute, distinct items upserted or held while
the page was quiet, newly proposed amendments, and how the run ended: a pause,

as a new proposal. Words written before entering flow do not belong to the slip.

`house-store.ts` serializes local edits, verifies IndexedDB writes and emits

Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

### Purpose

Resolve one stable target, run two independent assessments, synthesize a design critique, persist a snapshot, and ask the user what to improve next. The chat response is the primary deliverable; the snapshot is an archive/backlog for future commands.

### Hard Invariants

- Assessment A (design review) and Assessment B (detector/browser evidence) are both required.
- Assessment A must finish before detector findings enter the parent synthesis context. Detector output is deterministic, but it still anchors judgment.
- If sub-agents are unavailable, fall back sequentially: finish and record Assessment A first, then run Assessment B, then synthesize.
- A skipped detector is a failed critique run unless `detect.mjs` is missing or crashes after a real attempt.
- Viewable targets require browser inspection when available.
- Any local server started only for critique visualization must run in the background, have a recorded stop method, and be stopped before final reporting unless the user asks to keep it.
- Do not claim a user-visible overlay exists unless script injection succeeded and the detector ran in the page.

### Setup

1. **Resolve the target** to a concrete file path or URL. Prefer a source path over a dev-server URL when both identify the same surface; ports drift, paths do not.
   - "the homepage" -> `site/pages/index.astro` or `index.html`
   - "the settings modal" -> the primary component file
   - "this page" -> the current URL or source file
2. **Compute the slug**:
   ```bash
   node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/critique-storage.mjs slug "<resolved-path-or-url>"
   ```
   Keep it. If the command exits non-zero, skip persistence and trend for this run, but continue the critique.
3. **Read `.impeccable/critique/ignore.md`** if it exists. Drop matching findings silently; it is the only prior-run input critique consumes.

### Assessment Orchestration

Delegate Assessment A and Assessment B to separate sub-agents when possible. They must not see each other's output. Do not show findings to the user until synthesis.

Codex sub-agent gate:
- If `spawn_agent` is exposed and the user explicitly allowed sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work, spawn A and B immediately.
- If `spawn_agent` is exposed but the user did not explicitly allow sub-agents, ask exactly once: "Impeccable critique is designed to run two independent sub-agents for an unanchored assessment. May I use sub-agents for this critique?" Then stop until the user answers.
- If allowed, spawn A and B. If declined, run sequentially and report `Assessment independence: degraded (sub-agents declined by user)`.
- If `spawn_agent` is not exposed, do not ask; run sequentially and report `Assessment independence: degraded (spawn_agent unavailable in this session)`.
- If spawning fails after permission, run sequentially and report `Assessment independence: degraded (sub-agent spawn failed: <exact error>)`.
Prefer `fork_context: false` with self-contained prompts containing cwd, target, live URL, references, product context, and output contract. If using `fork_context: true`, omit `agent_type`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort`.

If browser automation is available, each assessment creates its own new tab. Never reuse an existing tab, even if it is already at the right URL.

### Assessment A: Design Review

Read relevant source files and visually inspect the live page when browser automation is available. Think like a design director.

Evaluate:
- **AI slop**: Would someone believe "AI made this" immediately? Check all DON'T guidance from the parent Impeccable skill.
- **Holistic design**: hierarchy, IA, emotional fit, discoverability, composition, typography, color, accessibility, states, copy, and edge cases.
- **Cognitive load**: consult the [Cognitive Load Assessment](#cognitive-load-assessment) section below; report checklist failures and decision points with >4 visible options.
- **Emotional journey**: peak-end rule, emotional valleys, reassurance at high-stakes moments.
- **Nielsen heuristics**: consult the [Heuristics Scoring Guide](#heuristics-scoring-guide) section below; score all 10 heuristics 0-4.

Return: AI slop verdict, heuristic scores, cognitive load, emotional journey, 2-3 strengths, 3-5 priority issues, persona red flags, minor observations, and provocative questions.

### Assessment B: Detector + Browser Evidence

Run the bundled detector and browser visualization evidence. Assessment B is mandatory and must remain isolated from Assessment A until both are complete.

CLI scan:
```bash
node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/detect.mjs --json [target]
```

- Pass markup files/directories as `[target]`; do not pass CSS-only files.
- For URLs, skip CLI scan and use browser visualization.
- For very large trees (500+ scannable files), narrow scope or ask.
- Exit code 0 = clean; 2 = findings.
- If the detector entrypoint is missing or fails to load, report deterministic scan unavailable and continue with browser/manual review.

Browser visualization is required for a viewable target when browser automation is available. Use a localhost dev/static URL for local files; avoid `file://` unless the available browser explicitly supports this workflow. Overlay flow:

1. Create a fresh tab and navigate.
2. Preflight mutable injection by setting `document.title` and appending a `<script>` tag. Read-only evaluate APIs do not count.
3. If mutation is unavailable, skip live server, browser presentation, and injection; report fallback signal.
4. If mutation is available, start `node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/live-server.mjs --background`, present the browser if supported, label `[Human]`, scroll top, inject `http://localhost:PORT/detect.js`, wait 2-3 seconds, read `impeccable` console messages, then stop the live server.
5. For multi-view targets, inject on 3-5 representative pages.

Codex Browser note: Use the Browser skill. Do not spend a Browser attempt on `file://`. Only call `visibility.set(true)` after mutable script injection is confirmed for the `[Human]` overlay path; verify with `get()`. Use `tab.dev.logs({ filter: "impeccable" })` for console results. Its Playwright `evaluate(...)` surface is read-only; do not rely on it for mutation.

Return: CLI findings JSON/counts, browser console findings if applicable, false positives, and skipped/failed browser steps with concrete reasons.

After Assessment B returns usable CLI findings, reuse them. Do not rerun `detect.mjs` in the parent unless Assessment B failed, was truncated, or omitted count, rule names, or file locations.

Codex failure accounting: final Run Notes must include target slug, ignore list, assessment independence, CLI detector, browser visibility, overlay injection, live-server cleanup, temp-file cleanup, and any fallback signal used. Do not run repo status checks, late API spelunking, or unrelated verification after the report is assembled.

### Generate Combined Critique Report

Synthesize both assessments into a single report. Do NOT simply concatenate. Weave the findings together, noting where the LLM review and detector agree, where the detector caught issues the LLM missed, and where detector findings are false positives.

The chat response is the primary user-facing deliverable. Present the full structured critique below in chat; do not replace it with a summary and a link. The persisted snapshot is only an archive/backlog for later commands.

Codex final-answer note: `$impeccable critique` produces a report artifact, so the final chat response should intentionally exceed the usual concise close-out style. Do not title the final response "Critique Summary" unless the user explicitly asked for a summary.

Structure your feedback as a design director would:

#### Design Health Score
> *Consult the [Heuristics Scoring Guide](#heuristics-scoring-guide) section below.*

Present the Nielsen's 10 heuristics scores as a table:

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key Issue |
|---|-----------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | Visibility of System Status | ? | [specific finding or "n/a" if solid] |
| 2 | Match System / Real World | ? | |
| 3 | User Control and Freedom | ? | |
| 4 | Consistency and Standards | ? | |
| 5 | Error Prevention | ? | |
| 6 | Recognition Rather Than Recall | ? | |
| 7 | Flexibility and Efficiency | ? | |
| 8 | Aesthetic and Minimalist Design | ? | |
| 9 | Error Recovery | ? | |
| 10 | Help and Documentation | ? | |
| **Total** | | **??/40** | **[Rating band]** |

Be honest with scores. A 4 means genuinely excellent. Most real interfaces score 20-32.

#### Anti-Patterns Verdict

**Start here.** Does this look AI-generated?

**LLM assessment**: Your own evaluation of AI slop tells. Cover overall aesthetic feel, layout sameness, generic composition, missed opportunities for personality.

**Deterministic scan**: Summarize what the automated detector found, with counts and file locations. Note any additional issues the detector caught that you missed, and flag any false positives.

**Visual overlays** (if injection succeeded): Tell the user that overlays are now visible in the **[Human]** tab in their browser, highlighting the detected issues. Summarize what the console output reported. If browser visualization was attempted but injection failed, say that no reliable user-visible overlay is available and report the fallback signal instead.

#### Overall Impression
A brief gut reaction: what works, what doesn't, and the single biggest opportunity.

#### What's Working
Highlight 2-3 things done well. Be specific about why they work.

#### Priority Issues
The 3-5 most impactful design problems, ordered by importance.

For each issue, tag with **P0-P3 severity** (see [Issue Severity below](#issue-severity-p0p3) for definitions):
- **[P?] What**: Name the problem clearly
- **Why it matters**: How this hurts users or undermines goals
- **Fix**: What to do about it (be concrete)
- **Suggested command**: Which command could address this (from: $impeccable adapt, $impeccable animate, $impeccable audit, $impeccable bolder, $impeccable clarify, $impeccable colorize, $impeccable critique, $impeccable delight, $impeccable distill, $impeccable document, $impeccable harden, $impeccable layout, $impeccable onboard, $impeccable optimize, $impeccable overdrive, $impeccable polish, $impeccable quieter, $impeccable shape, $impeccable typeset)

#### Persona Red Flags
> *Consult the [Personas reference](#persona-based-design-testing) below.*

Auto-select 2-3 personas most relevant to this interface type (use the selection table in the reference). If `AGENTS.md` contains a `## Design Context` section from `impeccable init`, also generate 1-2 project-specific personas from the audience/brand info.

For each selected persona, walk through the primary user action and list specific red flags found:

**Alex (Power User)**: No keyboard shortcuts detected. Form requires 8 clicks for primary action. Forced modal onboarding. High abandonment risk.

**Jordan (First-Timer)**: Icon-only nav in sidebar. Technical jargon in error messages ("404 Not Found"). No visible help. Will abandon at step 2.

Be specific. Name the exact elements and interactions that fail each persona. Don't write generic persona descriptions; write what broke for them.

#### Minor Observations
Quick notes on smaller issues worth addressing.

#### Questions to Consider
Provocative questions that might unlock better solutions:
- "What if the primary action were more prominent?"
- "Does this need to feel this complex?"
- "What would a confident version of this look like?"

#### Run Notes
Keep this compact. Include status for target slug, ignore list, assessment independence, CLI detector, browser visibility, overlay injection, live server cleanup, and temp-file cleanup. For failed or skipped steps, give the concrete observed reason and the fallback signal used. In the final chat response, also include snapshot write and trend read status after persistence has run.

Codex Run Notes are final-chat only. Do not include this section in the persisted snapshot body, because persistence, trend read, and temp cleanup happen after the snapshot write and would otherwise archive stale status such as "pending after persistence."

**Remember**:
- Be direct. Vague feedback wastes everyone's time.
- Be specific. "The submit button," not "some elements."
- Say what's wrong AND why it matters to users.
- Give concrete suggestions. Cut "consider exploring..." entirely.
- Prioritize ruthlessly. If everything is important, nothing is.
- Don't soften criticism. Developers need honest feedback to ship great design.

### Persist the Snapshot

Once the report above is finalized, write it to `.impeccable/critique/` so the user can refer back, and so `$impeccable polish` can pick up the priority issues without a copy-paste.

Skip this step if the Setup slug was null (vague or root-level target).

1. **Write the body to a temp file** so you can pipe it to the helper. Use the full critique report (heuristic table, anti-patterns verdict, priority issues, persona red flags, minor observations, and questions), but stop before the "Ask the User" / "Recommended Actions" sections that come later.

   Codex: exclude Run Notes from the temp body file; Run Notes are final-chat only because persistence, trend read, and temp cleanup happen after the snapshot write.

2. **Pass the structured metadata** through `IMPECCABLE_CRITIQUE_META` (JSON), then run the write command:
   ```bash
   IMPECCABLE_CRITIQUE_META='{"target":"<user phrasing>","total_score":<n>,"p0_count":<n>,"p1_count":<n>}' \
     node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/critique-storage.mjs write <slug> <body-file>
   ```
   The helper prints the absolute path it wrote.

3. **Delete the temp body file** after the write attempt completes, whether the write succeeded or failed. If deletion fails, mention `temp-file cleanup failed: <reason>` briefly in the final output, but do not block the critique.

4. **Read the trend** for context:
   ```bash
   node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/critique-storage.mjs trend <slug> 5
   ```
   This returns a JSON array of the last 5 frontmatter entries (including the one you just wrote).

5. **Append a single line to the user-visible output**, after the report and before the questions:

   > **Trend for `<slug>` (last 5 runs): 24 → 28 → 32 → 29 → 32**
   > Wrote `.impeccable/critique/<filename>`.

   If this is the first run for the slug, the trend is just one score; say so: "First run for this target, no trend yet."

This is fire-and-forget. Do not show the user the helper's JSON output; only the human-readable trend line and the written path. Failures here should not block the rest of the flow; print the error and move on.

### Ask the User

**After presenting findings**, use targeted questions based on what was actually found. STOP and use Codex's structured user-input/question tool when available; if unavailable, ask directly in chat to clarify what you cannot infer. These answers will shape the action plan.

Ask questions along these lines (adapt to the specific findings; do NOT ask generic questions):

1. **Priority direction**: Based on the issues found, ask which category matters most to the user right now. For example: "I found problems with visual hierarchy, color usage, and information overload. Which area should we tackle first?" Offer the top 2-3 issue categories as options.

2. **Design intent**: If the critique found a tonal mismatch, ask whether it was intentional. For example: "The interface feels clinical and corporate. Is that the intended tone, or should it feel warmer/bolder/more playful?" Offer 2-3 tonal directions as options based on what would fix the issues found.

1	# The House and the fluid desk
     2	
     3	The manuscript remains the centre of the workspace. Comments, editorial notes,
     4	sources, books, records and connections to past writing share its margins. The
     5	existing side panels remain available for deliberate browsing.
     6	
     7	[Names & inheritance](#names-and-inheritance) · [Margin interactions](#interaction-contract) ·
     8	[Focus & assistance](#focus-and-assistance) · [Storage & sync](#storage-and-sync) ·
     9	[Verification](#verification)
    10	
    11	## Names and inheritance
    12	
    13	| Name       | Meaning                                                                                                                   |
    14	| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    15	| House      | The writer's reusable defaults and standards.                                                                             |
    16	| Collection | A series of folios sharing context. A folio belongs to at most one collection.                                            |
    17	| Folio      | One piece of writing, with its own dossier.                                                                               |
    18	| Dossier    | Audience, purpose, form, tone, constraints and supporting material for a piece. `ProjectBrief` is the internal type name. |
    19	| Charter    | Required or preferred standards, scoped to the House, collection or folio.                                                |
    20	| Edition    | A saved version of the dossier.                                                                                           |
    21	| Amendment  | A proposed change prompted by the draft, applied only when the writer files it.                                           |
    22	| Register   | The history of context changes and their provenance.                                                                      |
    23	
    24	```mermaid
    25	flowchart LR
    26	    house[House defaults] --> collection[Collection context]
    27	    collection --> folio[Folio dossier]
    28	    folio --> context[Effective model context]
    29	    charter[Applicable charter articles] --> context
    30	    amendment[Filed amendment] --> folio
    31	```
    32	
    33	**Fields inherit; standards accumulate.** Nonempty folio fields override collection fields, which override House fields.
    34	Working titles belong only to folios. Legacy interview stand-ins yield to shared
    35	context; blank fields inherit. Charters accumulate across all applicable scopes.
    36	A later manual edit supersedes an earlier amendment's provenance.
    37	
    38	`/house/` exposes the cabinet, the register and developer diagnostics. Links from
    39	the Library, the folio menu and dossier refinement keep the active folio in view.
    40	The context preview shows inherited fields and standards; individual tools add
    41	their own instructions, excerpts and source material. Token counts are estimates.
    42	
    43	`loadModelBriefForFolio` creates a read-only effective dossier for review, research,
    44	the editorial room and contextual tools. It never saves inherited values into the
    45	folio. Editing, export and edition history continue to use the original dossier.
    46	House changes refresh active model context; applying an amendment refreshes the
    47	saved dossier too.
    48	
    49	### Inspect the context
    50	
    51	| In the House | What you can inspect                                                            |
    52	| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    53	| Cabinet      | House defaults, collection membership, folio fields and their layer provenance. |
    54	| Register     | What changed, its source, its previous value and its reason.                    |
    55	| Engine room  | Learned timing, local flow sessions and model decision diagnostics.             |
    56	
    57	## Interaction contract
    58	
    59	- Hovering or focusing a passage marker reveals its associated margin card and
    60	  connections. Clicking a comment or persona note unfolds its full conversation
    61	  in that margin slot. Suggestions use the same placement service.
    62	- One conversation owns the foreground at a time. Switching preserves separate
    63	  unsent reply drafts for the mounted editor session; reloading does not preserve
    64	  those unsent drafts. Sent replies retain the existing storage behavior.
    65	- On narrow screens or with automatic margin reading disabled, the existing
    66	  anchored card provides the fallback. Ambient dock cards yield to open threads,
    67	  tools and selection actions. Open margin cards adapt to viewport changes.
    68	- Cards follow document scrolling and step around tools and expanded threads.
    69	  Escape closes the active conversation. Selection actions yield while a thread
    70	  or suggestion is open.
    71	- Fallback comment, persona-note and suggestion cards follow their passage too.
    72	  A passive listener on the manuscript scroller and resize/reflow updates share
    73	  one animation frame. Cards without a margin slot tuck below or above the live
    74	  passage; slot conversations keep the existing margin handshake. A passage fully
    75	  outside the visible manuscript closes a fallback card without a pin or draft.
    76	  Pinned notes and unsent drafts stay clamped on screen. Split marks count as
    77	  visible while any fragment remains in view.
    78	- Manual focus remains available. Automatic focus fades workspace chrome without
    79	  collapsing the writer's side panels. Interacting with controls or a conversation
    80	  prevents automatic focus from hiding them. A manual exit overrides automatic
    81	  focus temporarily.
    82	
    83	## Focus and assistance
    84	
    85	`flow-state.ts` reads typing cadence; `flow-profile.ts` learns pause thresholds and
    86	item preferences locally. Working shows a small selection, settling holds new
    87	items, flow clears ambient cards, and stuck favors one relevant item plus its
    88	connections. `flow-conductor.ts` combines these signals with budgeted Jev calls.
    89	Local connections are candidates, not claims of semantic certainty. Drift checks
    90	propose amendments rather than silently rewriting the dossier.
    91	
    92	| Reading  | What the margin does                          |
    93	| -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
    94	| Working  | Offers a small selection of relevant items.   |
    95	| Settling | Keeps existing items and holds new arrivals.  |
    96	| Flow     | Clears ambient cards and holds arrivals.      |
    97	| Stuck    | Favors one relevant item and its connections. |
    98	
    99	### Galley slips
   100	
   101	Entering `flow` opens a session. Leaving for any other reading closes it; Escape,
   102	reaching for the room, turning focus off, disabling automatic focus, destroying
   103	the editor or changing folios closes it too. A session worth remembering lasts
   104	at least one minute **or** adds forty net words. Shorter runs leave no slip.
   105	
   106	The slip records its folio, start and end, time in flow, net document word growth
   107	(never negative), rounded words per minute, distinct items upserted or held while
   108	the page was quiet, newly proposed amendments, and how the run ended: a pause,
   109	reaching, a manual exit, stepping away, or closing the folio. Repeated updates to
   110	the same item count once; an amendment already waiting before flow does not count
   111	as a new proposal. Words written before entering flow do not belong to the slip.
   112	
   113	The conductor announces qualifying slips on `twyne:flow-session` and logs them as
   114	focus decisions. The last thirty are saved as plain objects in IndexedDB meta
   115	`flow-sessions`; no Qwik store proxies enter that history. `loadFlowSessions()`
   116	reads it and `FlowController.lastSession()` restores the latest slip for the
   117	current folio after a remount. The House's Engine room lists recent slips by date,
   118	folio, minutes, words, pace, what waited and how the run ended; its JSON export
   119	includes them. Slips and cadence profiles remain on this device.
   120	
   121	On a narrow screen the slip starts as a compact receipt; open it to see the
   122	details or file it to clear the corner. A relevant margin card takes priority
   123	over the receipt, and opening a conversation clears ambient dock furniture.
   124	The ink ribbon stays beside the word count as the manuscript scrolls. Its
   125	reading has a text alternative and does not announce changes while you write.
   126	
   127	### A way in, and the pneumatic post
   128	
   129	While stuck, Jev's unresolved-passage Noul must reach 0.6 before a single **A way
   130	in** item is offered. In the same budgeted request, a Choice selects a short prompt
   131	from fixed options: say it plainly, start with a concrete detail, return to the
   132	audience and purpose, pick up an earlier thread, or leave TK and move on. Code
   133	supplies the wording from templates and the dossier; System One selects rather
   134	than writes prose. The earlier-thread option needs an actual matched echo, and
   135	the card links the best available echo for its passage.
   136	
   137	With no client, a local stuck reading can supply the plain-sentence prompt only
   138	after strong churn (at least 0.6) and the writer's learned stuck pause. A configured
   139	client's budget skip or failed judgement does not count as confirmation. Late
   140	answers cannot offer help after the passage or mode changes. Only one way-in item
   141	is live at once; dismissing it keeps it dismissed for that passage during the
   142	mounted conductor session. It leads while stuck and waits, with an explicit
   143	policy reason, in every other reading or at another passage.
   144	
   145	`FlowSnapshot.heldKinds` is the pneumatic post's tally: held items by kind, beside
   146	the total `held`. It includes only policy-held items, including a waiting way in;
   147	dismissed items do not count. The margin can name what is waiting without showing
   148	the cards during a quiet run.
   149	
   150	Cover lookups can be disabled in review controls. Book titles go to Open Library;
   151	record titles go to MusicBrainz and covers come from the Cover Art Archive.
   152	Cadence profiles stay on this device. Diagnostics may contain draft excerpts,
   153	titles, dossier changes and model decisions: inspect an export before sharing it.
   154	
   155	## Storage and sync
   156	
   157	`house-store.ts` serializes local edits, verifies IndexedDB writes and emits
   158	`twyne:house-changed`. Each edit advances the whole snapshot's timestamp, including
   159	collection membership changes and withdrawals. House state sync runs on both the
   160	House page and the editor, with a live Convex subscription and reconnect refresh.
   161	
   162	House, collections and charter use the newer complete snapshot; this is
   163	last-write-wins, not a per-field collaborative merge. Ledger entries are unioned
   164	by ID. A stale server upload may contribute history but cannot replace a newer
   165	snapshot. Local history retains 500 entries; server history is paginated. Signed-out
   166	writing remains local. The current local House is shared within the browser profile,
   167	as with the existing local folio store.
   168	
   169	Ledger acknowledgements are tracked per account in IndexedDB, separately from
   170	the server's bounded history window. An acknowledged entry is not uploaded again
   171	just because it is absent from the latest pull. Partial uploads retry only the
   172	unacknowledged batches; persisting an acknowledgement can retry without repeating
   173	the accepted server mutation.
   174	
   175	The margin handshake lives in `margin-surface.ts`: a card reserves a slot before
   176	the editor mounts its full conversation, then receives geometry updates. Pending
   177	reservations survive the old card closing. Editor request tokens prevent slower
   178	opens from replacing a more recently selected conversation.
   179	
   180	### Source map
   181	
   182	| Contract                           | Implementation                                                                                                              |
   183	| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   184	| Context assembly and provenance    | [`house-model.ts`](../src/utils/house-model.ts), [`model-context.ts`](../src/utils/model-context.ts)                        |
   185	| Local persistence and account sync | [`house-store.ts`](../src/utils/house-store.ts), [`house-sync.ts`](../src/utils/house-sync.ts)                              |
   186	| Cadence and learned preferences    | [`flow-state.ts`](../src/utils/flow-state.ts), [`flow-profile.ts`](../src/utils/flow-profile.ts)                            |
   187	| Gathering and surfacing            | [`flow-conductor.ts`](../src/components/editor/extensions/flow-conductor.ts), [`flow-items.ts`](../src/utils/flow-items.ts) |
   188	| Conversation placement             | [`margin-surface.ts`](../src/utils/margin-surface.ts), [`flow-surface.tsx`](../src/components/in-flow/flow-surface.tsx)     |
   189	
   190	## Verification
   191	
   192	Focused tests cover inheritance, provenance, quiet-mode surfacing, focus overrides,
   193	session qualification and history, teardown/remount, typed way-in selection and
   194	dismissal, held-kind tallies, cadence transitions and learned thresholds, margin
   195	registration, fallback viewport clamping, card collision placement, snapshot
   196	deletion semantics, account isolation and stale uploads. Browser checks exercise
   197	the House cabinet and tabs, comment/note/suggestion switching, separate reply
   198	drafts, Escape, scrolling and mobile resizing.
   199	
   200	**Separate integration checks:** a live authenticated two-device sync and a
   201	funded model-generation session. Local browser fixtures and mocked backend tests
   202	do not prove these paths.

   148	the cards during a quiet run.

   151	record titles go to MusicBrainz and covers come from the Cover Art Archive.
   152	Cadence profiles stay on this device. Diagnostics may contain draft excerpts,

    10	
    11	## Names and inheritance
    12	
    13	| Name       | Meaning                                                                                                                   |
    14	| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    15	| House      | The writer's reusable defaults and standards.                                                                             |

    19	| Charter    | Required or preferred standards, scoped to the House, collection or folio.                                                |
    20	| Edition    | A saved version of the dossier.                                                                                           |
    21	| Amendment  | A proposed change prompted by the draft, applied only when the writer files it.                                           |
    22	| Register   | The history of context changes and their provenance.                                                                      |
    23	
    24	```mermaid
    25	flowchart LR
    26	    house[House defaults] --> collection[Collection context]
    27	    collection --> folio[Folio dossier]
    28	    folio --> context[Effective model context]
    29	    charter[Applicable charter articles] --> context
    30	    amendment[Filed amendment] --> folio

    33	**Fields inherit; standards accumulate.** Nonempty folio fields override collection fields, which override House fields.
    34	Working titles belong only to folios. Legacy interview stand-ins yield to shared
    35	context; blank fields inherit. Charters accumulate across all applicable scopes.

    52	| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

    56	
    57	## Interaction contract
    58	
    59	- Hovering or focusing a passage marker reveals its associated margin card and
    60	  connections. Clicking a comment or persona note unfolds its full conversation
    61	  in that margin slot. Suggestions use the same placement service.
    62	- One conversation owns the foreground at a time. Switching preserves separate
    63	  unsent reply drafts for the mounted editor session; reloading does not preserve
    64	  those unsent drafts. Sent replies retain the existing storage behavior.
    65	- On narrow screens or with automatic margin reading disabled, the existing
    66	  anchored card provides the fallback. Ambient dock cards yield to open threads,
    67	  tools and selection actions. Open margin cards adapt to viewport changes.
    68	- Cards follow document scrolling and step around tools and expanded threads.
    69	  Escape closes the active conversation. Selection actions yield while a thread
    70	  or suggestion is open.
    71	- Fallback comment, persona-note and suggestion cards follow their passage too.
    72	  A passive listener on the manuscript scroller and resize/reflow updates share
    73	  one animation frame. Cards without a margin slot tuck below or above the live

    75	  outside the visible manuscript closes a fallback card without a pin or draft.
    76	  Pinned notes and unsent drafts stay clamped on screen. Split marks count as
    77	  visible while any fragment remains in view.
    78	- Manual focus remains available. Automatic focus fades workspace chrome without
    79	  collapsing the writer's side panels. Interacting with controls or a conversation
    80	  prevents automatic focus from hiding them. A manual exit overrides automatic
    81	  focus temporarily.

    84	
    85	`flow-state.ts` reads typing cadence; `flow-profile.ts` learns pause thresholds and

    90	propose amendments rather than silently rewriting the dossier.

1	# Fluid editor + the House context model
     2	
     3	## Context
     4	
     5	Twyne already has most of the parts of a "fluid" editor, but each decides on its own when to appear:
     6	- the struggle tracker opens one margin tool when a paragraph looks stuck (`extensions/struggle-tracker.ts`)
     7	- background research files sources (`utils/background-research.ts`)
     8	- comments and persona notes sit in the Editorial Board side panel
     9	- zen mode is manual only (the `twyne:zen-mode` event)
    10	
    11	The writer still has to open panels to see things. The goal is that everything reaches the writer in the flow of writing, with nothing opened by hand:
    12	- The app reads whether you are **in flow, working, or stuck**. Jev confirms the borderline cases.
    13	- It goes quiet in flow and fades into zen mode on its own.
    14	- When you're stuck, it brings forward the single most useful item:
    15	  - a comment or persona reply as it streams in
    16	  - a source
    17	  - a book or album card with its cover
    18	  - a passage from your other work
    19	  - a charter standard you're breaking
    20	- Hovering a comment draws arrows to the passages and cards it connects to.
    21	- It learns your rhythms and which kinds of help you actually use.
    22	
    23	Second request, same underlying need: the data model has no clear hierarchy or language.
    24	- Dossiers and briefs are the same thing under two names.
    25	- There's no grouping above a single folio.
    26	- There are no standards that follow you across pieces.
    27	- The dossier is fixed once filed, even though intent changes as you write.
    28	
    29	User decisions:
    30	- **Names:** French editorial house language.
    31	- **Sync:** collections, charters and the ledger go into Convex tables now.
    32	- **Cover lookups:** on by default, with a switch.
    33	
    34	## The language (goes into UI copy, docs, and code names)
    35	
    36	| Term | What it is |
    37	|---|---|
    38	| **House** | The writer. Holds the house charter and default dossier fields. One per account. |
    39	| **Collection** | A series of folios, like a publisher's *collection* (Série noire). Holds a shared dossier layer and a collection charter. |
    40	| **Folio** | One piece of writing. Unchanged. |
    41	| **Dossier** | What a piece is for: audience, goal, tone, constraints, references. The internal type stays `ProjectBrief`; "brief" is retired from UI copy. |
    42	| **Charter** | Standards and requirements. Each item is a short rule with a severity (*must* or *prefer*) and a scope. Charters stack from House to Collection to Folio. |
    43	| **Edition** | A filed version of a dossier. Already exists (`utils/brief-history.ts`). |
    44	| **Revision** | A version of the manuscript text. Already exists (Lix). |
    45	| **Amendment** | A change to the dossier that the draft proposes ("your pages now read for practitioners"). The writer files it, amends it, or sets it aside. Filing one creates an Edition. |
    46	| **Context stack** | House, then Collection, then Folio dossier, then filed amendments, then the current moment. This is exactly what the models receive. |
    47	| **Ledger** | An append-only log of every context change: who or what made it, when, and why. |
    48	
    49	A revision changes the words. An edition changes what the words are for.
    50	
    51	## Part A — the flow layer
    52	
    53	### New pure modules (unit-tested, no DOM)
    54	
    55	- **`src/utils/flow-state.ts`** reads flow from typing cadence.
    56	  - Input: keystroke samples (time, inserted, deleted), pointer and panel activity, and the struggle score from `readStruggle` (`utils/struggle-signals.ts`).
    57	  - Output: `flow | working | stuck | away`.
    58	  - Hysteresis: entering flow needs sustained steady typing (a minimum active ratio and a low delete ratio over a window). Leaving flow needs a real pause, a move to the margin or masthead, or Escape.
    59	  - An intermediate `settling` stage dims the chrome before full zen.
    60	  - Thresholds come from the profile, not constants.
    61	- **`src/utils/flow-profile.ts`** learns the writer's patterns.
    62	  - Rolling samples of burst length, pause length, and the time it takes to reach flow.
    63	  - Hour-of-day writing histogram.
    64	  - Per item-kind engagement counts: `shown`, `engaged`, `dismissed`, `ignored`.
    65	  - Derives `stuckPauseMs`, `flowEntryMs`, `exitPauseMs`, and `kindWeight(kind)`. The weight is Laplace-smoothed, so it starts neutral.
    66	  - Pure update functions, plus load and save through `loadMetaFromIdb`/`saveMetaToIdb` (`utils/idb.ts`).
    67	- **`src/utils/flow-items.ts`** defines the item model and the surfacing policy.
    68	  - `FlowItem` kinds: `tool | comment | persona-note | source | work (book/album/song/film) | shelf (dossier attachment / bibliography match) | echo (your other work) | charter | amendment`.
    69	  - Every item has anchor quotes, a priority, a timestamp, and optional `links` to other items and passages.
    70	  - `decideSurface(state, items, profile, cursor)` returns visible items, held items, and a reason for each:
    71	    - **flow:** nothing new appears; items are held.
    72	    - **working:** at most two cards near the viewport, plus ticks.
    73	    - **stuck:** the single best item for the cursor's paragraph, plus its links.
    74	  - Scoring: kind weight × proximity to the cursor paragraph × freshness × Jev relevance.
    75	  - Also exports `stackCards(desiredTops, heights, obstacles)` to avoid collisions in the margin.
    76	- **`src/utils/flow-connections.ts`** finds connections locally.
    77	  - Tokenizes and builds a small TF-IDF index over paragraphs from other folios (`loadFoliosFromIdb`, `loadFolioContentFromIdb`, `htmlToPlainText` from `utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`) and over the current manuscript.
    78	  - `relatedPassages(text, index, k)` returns candidates that Jev then confirms.
    79	  - `workCandidates(paragraph, marks)` pulls quoted or italic titles and research targets of kind `work` (`utils/research-targets.ts`).
    80	  - Also matches the paragraph against dossier attachments and bibliography entries (`utils/bibliography.ts`) for shelf items.
    81	- **`src/utils/flow-media.ts`** fetches covers.
    82	  - Books: OpenLibrary `search.json`, then `covers.openlibrary.org`.
    83	  - Albums and songs: MusicBrainz `ws/2/release-group` and `recording`, then `coverartarchive.org`.
    84	  - Only the title Jev picked is sent.
    85	  - Throttled to 1 request per second (MusicBrainz's limit), cached in IDB meta, and returns nothing when the switch is off.
    86	  - Cards show the title, creator, cover and a link, never lyric text.
    87	- **`src/utils/flow-diagnostics.ts`** keeps a ring buffer of the last 300 decisions and persists it to IDB meta, throttled.
    88	  - Each entry records: state transition and its signals, Jev request and answer, latency and budget, items surfaced or held with reasons, and the context-stack hash used.
    89	  - Emits `twyne:flow-diagnostics`.
    90	
    91	### Runtime
    92	
    93	- **`src/components/editor/extensions/flow-conductor.ts`** follows the lifecycle of `startInFlowTools`. It is started next to it in `twyne-editor.tsx` (around line 861), with the same `getClient`, `folioId` and brief.
    94	  - It feeds transactions and pointer events to `flow-state`.
    95	  - It asks Jev only at the edges, through `askJudgement` (`utils/judgement-client.ts`) and the shared budget in `utils/system-one-budget.ts`, batching several questions per request:
    96	    - "Is the writer in sustained composition, so interruptions should be withheld?" (noul)
    97	    - "Is the writer stuck?"
    98	    - "Does this candidate bear on the current paragraph?"
    99	    - "What kind of work is this title: book, album, song, film, or none?"
   100	    - "Is a charter standard breached here?"
   101	  - When Jev is unavailable, the local heuristics decide on their own.
   102	  - It gathers items from existing events without changing their producers:
   103	    - `IN_FLOW_EVENT`: the active tool
   104	    - `twyne:user-comments-changed` plus `loadUserComments` (`utils/user-comments.ts`)
   105	    - `twyne:persona-notes`
   106	    - `twyne:persona-reply-stream` and `twyne:persona-reply`: streaming text updates the card live
   107	    - `twyne:background-sources`, then a bibliography lookup
   108	  - Auto-zen dispatches `twyne:zen-mode` with `{on, source: "flow"}`. A manual toggle, with no source, sets a manual override that is respected for 10 minutes and recorded in the profile.
   109	  - It sets `document.documentElement.dataset.flow` so CSS can fade the chrome gradually.
   110	  - It publishes a snapshot on `twyne:flow`.
