     5	Twyne already has most of the parts of a "fluid" editor, but each decides on its own when to appear:
     6	- the struggle tracker opens one margin tool when a paragraph looks stuck (`extensions/struggle-tracker.ts`)
     7	- background research files sources (`utils/background-research.ts`)
     8	- comments and persona notes sit in the Editorial Board side panel
     9	- zen mode is manual only (the `twyne:zen-mode` event)
    10	
    11	The writer still has to open panels to see things. The goal is that everything reaches the writer in the flow of writing, with nothing opened by hand:
    12	- The app reads whether you are **in flow, working, or stuck**. Jev confirms the borderline cases.
    13	- It goes quiet in flow and fades into zen mode on its own.
    14	- When you're stuck, it brings forward the single most useful item:
    15	  - a comment or persona reply as it streams in
    16	  - a source
    17	  - a book or album card with its cover
    18	  - a passage from your other work
    19	  - a charter standard you're breaking
    20	- Hovering a comment draws arrows to the passages and cards it connects to.
    21	- It learns your rhythms and which kinds of help you actually use.
    22	
    23	Second request, same underlying need: the data model has no clear hierarchy or language.
    24	- Dossiers and briefs are the same thing under two names.
    25	- There's no grouping above a single folio.
    26	- There are no standards that follow you across pieces.
    27	- The dossier is fixed once filed, even though intent changes as you write.
    28	
    29	User decisions:
    30	- **Names:** French editorial house language.
    31	- **Sync:** collections, charters and the ledger go into Convex tables now.
    32	- **Cover lookups:** on by default, with a switch.
    33	
    34	## The language (goes into UI copy, docs, and code names)
    35	
    36	| Term | What it is |
    37	|---|---|
    38	| **House** | The writer. Holds the house charter and default dossier fields. One per account. |
    39	| **Collection** | A series of folios, like a publisher's *collection* (Série noire). Holds a shared dossier layer and a collection charter. |
    40	| **Folio** | One piece of writing. Unchanged. |
    41	| **Dossier** | What a piece is for: audience, goal, tone, constraints, references. The internal type stays `ProjectBrief`; "brief" is retired from UI copy. |
    42	| **Charter** | Standards and requirements. Each item is a short rule with a severity (*must* or *prefer*) and a scope. Charters stack from House to Collection to Folio. |
    43	| **Edition** | A filed version of a dossier. Already exists (`utils/brief-history.ts`). |
    44	| **Revision** | A version of the manuscript text. Already exists (Lix). |
    45	| **Amendment** | A change to the dossier that the draft proposes ("your pages now read for practitioners"). The writer files it, amends it, or sets it aside. Filing one creates an Edition. |
    46	| **Context stack** | House, then Collection, then Folio dossier, then filed amendments, then the current moment. This is exactly what the models receive. |
    47	| **Ledger** | An append-only log of every context change: who or what made it, when, and why. |
    48	
    49	A revision changes the words. An edition changes what the words are for.

    51	## Part A — the flow layer
    52	
    53	### New pure modules (unit-tested, no DOM)
    54	
    55	- **`src/utils/flow-state.ts`** reads flow from typing cadence.
    56	  - Input: keystroke samples (time, inserted, deleted), pointer and panel activity, and the struggle score from `readStruggle` (`utils/struggle-signals.ts`).
    57	  - Output: `flow | working | stuck | away`.
    58	  - Hysteresis: entering flow needs sustained steady typing (a minimum active ratio and a low delete ratio over a window). Leaving flow needs a real pause, a move to the margin or masthead, or Escape.
    59	  - An intermediate `settling` stage dims the chrome before full zen.
    60	  - Thresholds come from the profile, not constants.
    61	- **`src/utils/flow-profile.ts`** learns the writer's patterns.
    62	  - Rolling samples of burst length, pause length, and the time it takes to reach flow.
    63	  - Hour-of-day writing histogram.
    64	  - Per item-kind engagement counts: `shown`, `engaged`, `dismissed`, `ignored`.
    65	  - Derives `stuckPauseMs`, `flowEntryMs`, `exitPauseMs`, and `kindWeight(kind)`. The weight is Laplace-smoothed, so it starts neutral.
    66	  - Pure update functions, plus load and save through `loadMetaFromIdb`/`saveMetaToIdb` (`utils/idb.ts`).
    67	- **`src/utils/flow-items.ts`** defines the item model and the surfacing policy.
    68	  - `FlowItem` kinds: `tool | comment | persona-note | source | work (book/album/song/film) | shelf (dossier attachment / bibliography match) | echo (your other work) | charter | amendment`.
    69	  - Every item has anchor quotes, a priority, a timestamp, and optional `links` to other items and passages.
    70	  - `decideSurface(state, items, profile, cursor)` returns visible items, held items, and a reason for each:
    71	    - **flow:** nothing new appears; items are held.
    72	    - **working:** at most two cards near the viewport, plus ticks.
    73	    - **stuck:** the single best item for the cursor's paragraph, plus its links.
    74	  - Scoring: kind weight × proximity to the cursor paragraph × freshness × Jev relevance.
    75	  - Also exports `stackCards(desiredTops, heights, obstacles)` to avoid collisions in the margin.
    76	- **`src/utils/flow-connections.ts`** finds connections locally.
    77	  - Tokenizes and builds a small TF-IDF index over paragraphs from other folios (`loadFoliosFromIdb`, `loadFolioContentFromIdb`, `htmlToPlainText` from `utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`) and over the current manuscript.
    78	  - `relatedPassages(text, index, k)` returns candidates that Jev then confirms.
    79	  - `workCandidates(paragraph, marks)` pulls quoted or italic titles and research targets of kind `work` (`utils/research-targets.ts`).
    80	  - Also matches the paragraph against dossier attachments and bibliography entries (`utils/bibliography.ts`) for shelf items.
    81	- **`src/utils/flow-media.ts`** fetches covers.
    82	  - Books: OpenLibrary `search.json`, then `covers.openlibrary.org`.
    83	  - Albums and songs: MusicBrainz `ws/2/release-group` and `recording`, then `coverartarchive.org`.
    84	  - Only the title Jev picked is sent.
    85	  - Throttled to 1 request per second (MusicBrainz's limit), cached in IDB meta, and returns nothing when the switch is off.
    86	  - Cards show the title, creator, cover and a link, never lyric text.
    87	- **`src/utils/flow-diagnostics.ts`** keeps a ring buffer of the last 300 decisions and persists it to IDB meta, throttled.
    88	  - Each entry records: state transition and its signals, Jev request and answer, latency and budget, items surfaced or held with reasons, and the context-stack hash used.
    89	  - Emits `twyne:flow-diagnostics`.

    91	### Runtime
    92	
    93	- **`src/components/editor/extensions/flow-conductor.ts`** follows the lifecycle of `startInFlowTools`. It is started next to it in `twyne-editor.tsx` (around line 861), with the same `getClient`, `folioId` and brief.
    94	  - It feeds transactions and pointer events to `flow-state`.
    95	  - It asks Jev only at the edges, through `askJudgement` (`utils/judgement-client.ts`) and the shared budget in `utils/system-one-budget.ts`, batching several questions per request:
    96	    - "Is the writer in sustained composition, so interruptions should be withheld?" (noul)
    97	    - "Is the writer stuck?"
    98	    - "Does this candidate bear on the current paragraph?"
    99	    - "What kind of work is this title: book, album, song, film, or none?"
   100	    - "Is a charter standard breached here?"
   101	  - When Jev is unavailable, the local heuristics decide on their own.
   102	  - It gathers items from existing events without changing their producers:
   103	    - `IN_FLOW_EVENT`: the active tool
   104	    - `twyne:user-comments-changed` plus `loadUserComments` (`utils/user-comments.ts`)
   105	    - `twyne:persona-notes`
   106	    - `twyne:persona-reply-stream` and `twyne:persona-reply`: streaming text updates the card live

   124	## Part B — the House context model
   125	
   126	(Convex details are filled in below from the data-model survey.)
   127	
   128	### Model and storage
   129	- **`src/utils/context-stack.ts`**
   130	  - Types: `House`, `Collection { id, name, folioIds, dossier: Partial<ProjectInterviewAnswers>, attachments, charterId }`, `Charter { id, scope: house|collection|folio, ownerId, items: CharterItem[] }`, `CharterItem { id, text, severity: must|prefer, kind?: length|citation|style|voice|other }`, `LedgerEntry { at, layer, field, from, to, source: interview|refine|amendment|collection|manual, reason }`.
   131	  - `assembleContextStack(folioId)` merges the layers. A field is inherited from Collection and House when the folio leaves it blank, and each field is tagged with the layer it came from.
   132	  - `contextForModels(stack)` returns the compact string plus a token estimate for each layer.
   133	  - `effectiveBrief(stack)` returns a `ProjectBrief`, so existing read-only consumers can use the merged view.
   134	- **Local first:** records live in IDB meta under `house`, `house-collections`, `charters` and `context-ledger`.
   135	  - Every write goes through `toStorable` (`utils/idb.ts:445`) and is read back to verify it.
   136	  - This avoids the known silent failure where a Qwik proxy causes a `DataCloneError` on an IDB write.
   137	- **Convex tables** (read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` first).
   138	  - Named to avoid confusion with the generic row-storage helper `convex/lib/collections.ts`.
   139	  - Lists are rows, not arrays, per the guidelines.
   140	  - Tables:
   141	    - `houses`: userId, dossierDefaults, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`
   142	    - `houseCollections`: userId, collectionId, name, dossier, charterNote, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`, `by_userId_and_collectionId`
   143	    - `collectionMembers`: userId, collectionId, folioId; indexed `by_userId_and_collectionId`, `by_userId_and_folioId`
   144	    - `charterItems`: userId, itemId, scope, ownerRef, text, severity, kind, order, updatedAt; indexed `by_userId`, `by_userId_and_ownerRef`
   145	    - `contextLedger`: userId, entryId, at, layer, ownerRef, field, from, to, source, reason; indexed `by_userId_and_at`, paginated
   146	- **`convex/house.ts`** follows the auth pattern in `convex/userComments.ts`.
   147	  - The owner is always `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity().tokenIdentifier`, never passed in as an argument.
   148	  - Functions: `getHouse` (the whole house: collections, members, charter items); `upsertHouse`, `upsertCollection`, `deleteCollection`, `setCollectionMembers`, `upsertCharterItem`, `deleteCharterItem`; `appendLedgerEntries` (idempotent on `entryId`); `listLedger` (paginated).

   150	- **Tests:** `convex/house.test.ts` in the `describeConvex` style of `convex/userComments.test.ts`, including a second identity that must not see the first writer's rows.
   151	- **Edition provenance:** `archiveBriefEdition` gains an optional `source` and `reason`, and writes a ledger entry.

   154	- **`src/utils/context-drift.ts`** (pure plus a runner) asks Jev every N new words, and only outside flow: "Does the recent writing still serve the dossier's stated goal / audience / tone?"

   158	- **Charter enforcement:** on a pause while *working*, the conductor asks Jev per applicable charter item (batched, *must* items first). A breach becomes a `charter` card anchored to the paragraph. This is how standards follow the writer across pieces.
   159

   161	- **`/context` route** (`src/routes/context/index.tsx`), in the Library's typewriter style (`dept-label`, `--font-typewriter`, `--font-display`, `btn-paper`). Tabs:

   165	  4. **Diagnostics** (developers; shown when `import.meta.env.DEV` or `?diagnostics=1`): conductor decisions, Jev calls with latency and answers, budget state, per-layer token estimates, flow-profile numbers, and a JSON export.
   166	- **`src/components/context/house-diagram.tsx`** is an inline SVG in the mid-century French editorial style:

   168	  - index-card drawers for Collections
   169	  - manila folders for Folios, with a clipped dossier sheet and a stamped charter
   170	  - carbon-copy stacks for Editions and Revisions
   171	  - It works in both themes with the existing color tokens. A compact version appears in the Library header.

1	# The House and the fluid desk
     2	
     3	The manuscript remains the centre of the workspace. Comments, editorial notes,
     4	sources, books, records and connections to past writing share its margins. The
     5	existing side panels remain available for deliberate browsing.
     6	
     7	[Names & inheritance](#names-and-inheritance) · [Margin interactions](#interaction-contract) ·
     8	[Focus & assistance](#focus-and-assistance) · [Storage & sync](#storage-and-sync) ·
     9	[Verification](#verification)
    10	
    11	## Names and inheritance
    12	
    13	| Name       | Meaning                                                                                                                   |
    14	| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    15	| House      | The writer's reusable defaults and standards.                                                                             |
    16	| Collection | A series of folios sharing context. A folio belongs to at most one collection.                                            |
    17	| Folio      | One piece of writing, with its own dossier.                                                                               |
    18	| Dossier    | Audience, purpose, form, tone, constraints and supporting material for a piece. `ProjectBrief` is the internal type name. |
    19	| Charter    | Required or preferred standards, scoped to the House, collection or folio.                                                |
    20	| Edition    | A saved version of the dossier.                                                                                           |
    21	| Amendment  | A proposed change prompted by the draft, applied only when the writer files it.                                           |
    22	| Register   | The history of context changes and their provenance.                                                                      |
    23	
    24	```mermaid
    25	flowchart LR
    26	    house[House defaults] --> collection[Collection context]
    27	    collection --> folio[Folio dossier]
    28	    folio --> context[Effective model context]
    29	    charter[Applicable charter articles] --> context
    30	    amendment[Filed amendment] --> folio
    31	```
    32	
    33	**Fields inherit; standards accumulate.** Nonempty folio fields override collection fields, which override House fields.
    34	Working titles belong only to folios. Legacy interview stand-ins yield to shared
    35	context; blank fields inherit. Charters accumulate across all applicable scopes.
    36	A later manual edit supersedes an earlier amendment's provenance.
    37	
    38	`/house/` exposes the cabinet, the register and developer diagnostics. Links from
    39	the Library, the folio menu and dossier refinement keep the active folio in view.
    40	The context preview shows inherited fields and standards; individual tools add
    41	their own instructions, excerpts and source material. Token counts are estimates.
    42	
    43	`loadModelBriefForFolio` creates a read-only effective dossier for review, research,
    44	the editorial room and contextual tools. It never saves inherited values into the
    45	folio. Editing, export and edition history continue to use the original dossier.
    46	House changes refresh active model context; applying an amendment refreshes the
    47	saved dossier too.
    48	
    49	### Inspect the context
    50	
    51	| In the House | What you can inspect                                                            |
    52	| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    53	| Cabinet      | House defaults, collection membership, folio fields and their layer provenance. |
    54	| Register     | What changed, its source, its previous value and its reason.                    |
    55	| Engine room  | Learned timing, local flow sessions and model decision diagnostics.             |
    56	
    57	## Interaction contract
    58	
    59	- Hovering or focusing a passage marker reveals its associated margin card and
    60	  connections. Clicking a comment or persona note unfolds its full conversation
    61	  in that margin slot. Suggestions use the same placement service.
    62	- One conversation owns the foreground at a time. Switching preserves separate
    63	  unsent reply drafts for the mounted editor session; reloading does not preserve
    64	  those unsent drafts. Sent replies retain the existing storage behavior.
    65	- On narrow screens or with automatic margin reading disabled, the existing
    66	  anchored card provides the fallback. Ambient dock cards yield to open threads,
    67	  tools and selection actions. Open margin cards adapt to viewport changes.
    68	- Cards follow document scrolling and step around tools and expanded threads.
    69	  Escape closes the active conversation. Selection actions yield while a thread
    70	  or suggestion is open.
    71	- Fallback comment, persona-note and suggestion cards follow their passage too.
    72	  A passive listener on the manuscript scroller and resize/reflow updates share
    73	  one animation frame. Cards without a margin slot tuck below or above the live
    74	  passage; slot conversations keep the existing margin handshake. A passage fully
    75	  outside the visible manuscript closes a fallback card without a pin or draft.
    76	  Pinned notes and unsent drafts stay clamped on screen. Split marks count as
    77	  visible while any fragment remains in view.
    78	- Manual focus remains available. Automatic focus fades workspace chrome without
    79	  collapsing the writer's side panels. Interacting with controls or a conversation
    80	  prevents automatic focus from hiding them. A manual exit overrides automatic
    81	  focus temporarily.
    82	
    83	## Focus and assistance
    84	
    85	`flow-state.ts` reads typing cadence; `flow-profile.ts` learns pause thresholds and
    86	item preferences locally. Working shows a small selection, settling holds new
    87	items, flow clears ambient cards, and stuck favors one relevant item plus its
    88	connections. `flow-conductor.ts` combines these signals with budgeted Jev calls.
    89	Local connections are candidates, not claims of semantic certainty. Drift checks
    90	propose amendments rather than silently rewriting the dossier.
    91	
    92	| Reading  | What the margin does                          |
    93	| -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
    94	| Working  | Offers a small selection of relevant items.   |
    95	| Settling | Keeps existing items and holds new arrivals.  |
    96	| Flow     | Clears ambient cards and holds arrivals.      |
    97	| Stuck    | Favors one relevant item and its connections. |
    98	
    99	### Galley slips
   100	
   101	Entering `flow` opens a session. Leaving for any other reading closes it; Escape,
   102	reaching for the room, turning focus off, disabling automatic focus, destroying
   103	the editor or changing folios closes it too. A session worth remembering lasts
   104	at least one minute **or** adds forty net words. Shorter runs leave no slip.
   105	
   106	The slip records its folio, start and end, time in flow, net document word growth
   107	(never negative), rounded words per minute, distinct items upserted or held while
   108	the page was quiet, newly proposed amendments, and how the run ended: a pause,
   109	reaching, a manual exit, stepping away, or closing the folio. Repeated updates to
   110	the same item count once; an amendment already waiting before flow does not count
   111	as a new proposal. Words written before entering flow do not belong to the slip.
   112	
   113	The conductor announces qualifying slips on `twyne:flow-session` and logs them as
   114	focus decisions. The last thirty are saved as plain objects in IndexedDB meta
   115	`flow-sessions`; no Qwik store proxies enter that history. `loadFlowSessions()`
   116	reads it and `FlowController.lastSession()` restores the latest slip for the
   117	current folio after a remount. The House's Engine room lists recent slips by date,
   118	folio, minutes, words, pace, what waited and how the run ended; its JSON export
   119	includes them. Slips and cadence profiles remain on this device.
   120	
   121	On a narrow screen the slip starts as a compact receipt; open it to see the
   122	details or file it to clear the corner. A relevant margin card takes priority
   123	over the receipt, and opening a conversation clears ambient dock furniture.
   124	The ink ribbon stays beside the word count as the manuscript scrolls. Its
   125	reading has a text alternative and does not announce changes while you write.
   126	
   127	### A way in, and the pneumatic post
   128	
   129	While stuck, Jev's unresolved-passage Noul must reach 0.6 before a single **A way
   130	in** item is offered. In the same budgeted request, a Choice selects a short prompt
   131	from fixed options: say it plainly, start with a concrete detail, return to the
   132	audience and purpose, pick up an earlier thread, or leave TK and move on. Code
   133	supplies the wording from templates and the dossier; System One selects rather
   134	than writes prose. The earlier-thread option needs an actual matched echo, and
   135	the card links the best available echo for its passage.
   136	
   137	With no client, a local stuck reading can supply the plain-sentence prompt only
   138	after strong churn (at least 0.6) and the writer's learned stuck pause. A configured
   139	client's budget skip or failed judgement does not count as confirmation. Late
   140	answers cannot offer help after the passage or mode changes. Only one way-in item
   141	is live at once; dismissing it keeps it dismissed for that passage during the
   142	mounted conductor session. It leads while stuck and waits, with an explicit
   143	policy reason, in every other reading or at another passage.
   144	
   145	`FlowSnapshot.heldKinds` is the pneumatic post's tally: held items by kind, beside
   146	the total `held`. It includes only policy-held items, including a waiting way in;
   147	dismissed items do not count. The margin can name what is waiting without showing
   148	the cards during a quiet run.
   149	
   150	Cover lookups can be disabled in review controls. Book titles go to Open Library;
   151	record titles go to MusicBrainz and covers come from the Cover Art Archive.
   152	Cadence profiles stay on this device. Diagnostics may contain draft excerpts,
   153	titles, dossier changes and model decisions: inspect an export before sharing it.
   154	
   155	## Storage and sync
   156	
   157	`house-store.ts` serializes local edits, verifies IndexedDB writes and emits
   158	`twyne:house-changed`. Each edit advances the whole snapshot's timestamp, including
   159	collection membership changes and withdrawals. House state sync runs on both the
   160	House page and the editor, with a live Convex subscription and reconnect refresh.
   161	
   162	House, collections and charter use the newer complete snapshot; this is
   163	last-write-wins, not a per-field collaborative merge. Ledger entries are unioned
   164	by ID. A stale server upload may contribute history but cannot replace a newer
   165	snapshot. Local history retains 500 entries; server history is paginated. Signed-out
   166	writing remains local. The current local House is shared within the browser profile,
   167	as with the existing local folio store.
   168	
   169	Ledger acknowledgements are tracked per account in IndexedDB, separately from
   170	the server's bounded history window. An acknowledged entry is not uploaded again
   171	just because it is absent from the latest pull. Partial uploads retry only the
   172	unacknowledged batches; persisting an acknowledgement can retry without repeating
   173	the accepted server mutation.
   174	
   175	The margin handshake lives in `margin-surface.ts`: a card reserves a slot before
   176	the editor mounts its full conversation, then receives geometry updates. Pending
   177	reservations survive the old card closing. Editor request tokens prevent slower
   178	opens from replacing a more recently selected conversation.
   179	
   180	### Source map
   181	
   182	| Contract                           | Implementation                                                                                                              |
   183	| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   184	| Context assembly and provenance    | [`house-model.ts`](../src/utils/house-model.ts), [`model-context.ts`](../src/utils/model-context.ts)                        |
   185	| Local persistence and account sync | [`house-store.ts`](../src/utils/house-store.ts), [`house-sync.ts`](../src/utils/house-sync.ts)                              |
   186	| Cadence and learned preferences    | [`flow-state.ts`](../src/utils/flow-state.ts), [`flow-profile.ts`](../src/utils/flow-profile.ts)                            |
   187	| Gathering and surfacing            | [`flow-conductor.ts`](../src/components/editor/extensions/flow-conductor.ts), [`flow-items.ts`](../src/utils/flow-items.ts) |
   188	| Conversation placement             | [`margin-surface.ts`](../src/utils/margin-surface.ts), [`flow-surface.tsx`](../src/components/in-flow/flow-surface.tsx)     |
   189	
   190	## Verification
   191	
   192	Focused tests cover inheritance, provenance, quiet-mode surfacing, focus overrides,
   193	session qualification and history, teardown/remount, typed way-in selection and
   194	dismissal, held-kind tallies, cadence transitions and learned thresholds, margin
   195	registration, fallback viewport clamping, card collision placement, snapshot
   196	deletion semantics, account isolation and stale uploads. Browser checks exercise
   197	the House cabinet and tabs, comment/note/suggestion switching, separate reply
   198	drafts, Escape, scrolling and mobile resizing.
   199	
   200	**Separate integration checks:** a live authenticated two-device sync and a
   201	funded model-generation session. Local browser fixtures and mocked backend tests
   202	do not prove these paths.

    41	| **Dossier** | What a piece is for: audience, goal, tone, constraints, references. The internal type stays `ProjectBrief`; "brief" is retired from UI copy. |
    42	| **Charter** | Standards and requirements. Each item is a short rule with a severity (*must* or *prefer*) and a scope. Charters stack from House to Collection to Folio. |

content.text:
**I think Claude found a strong direction for Twyne.** The fluid desk gives the product a coherent purpose: assistance should arrive where you’re writing, at a moment when it can help, and recede when you’re absorbed.

I reviewed its plan and session against the current implementation. The tree also includes substantial Codex follow-through and our finishing work, so the finished behavior is a shared result.

The strongest parts are:

- **A shared policy for attention.** Comments, sources, earlier writing and editorial suggestions now have rules for when they appear. That makes the margins feel like part of the writing environment. The quiet states and single foreground conversation are particularly good decisions. [Interaction contract](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/docs/flow-and-context.md:57)
- **The House gives context a useful structure.** Reusable defaults, collection context, folio overrides and visible provenance address a real problem: repeatedly explaining yourself to writing tools. Keeping inherited context separate from the saved dossier is a sound architectural choice. [Context inheritance](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/docs/flow-and-context.md:33)
- **Amendments preserve authorship.** A draft can reveal that its purpose has changed, and Twyne can propose updating the dossier. Having the writer explicitly file that change is a thoughtful distinction between changing the words and changing their intent.

My main criticism is that **the plan defines mechanisms more precisely than successful writing experiences**. It specifies cadence detection, relevance judgments, covers, arrows and diagnostics, but gives less attention to establishing whether an intervention was welcome or useful. [Claude’s plan](/home/diogenes/.claude/plans/goofy-enchanting-riddle.md:175)

That matters because the current adaptation remains fairly modest: pauses and deletion patterns influence state; opening and dismissing items influence their ranking. Careful revision can resemble struggle, and opening a card can reflect curiosity rather than usefulness. Jev adds another reading, but those interpretations still need validation. [Cadence policy](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/flow-state.ts:159), [preference learning](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/flow-profile.ts:152)

Visually, the editorial language suits Twyne. The pneumatic post has a clear function: something is waiting without demanding attention. I’m less convinced by giving pace and word growth much prominence in the galley slip. Cutting a paragraph can be the most valuable work of a session.

Where I’d take it next, in order:

1. **Make the attention behavior trustworthy.** Give interventions a concise explanation of why they appeared, an easy “later,” and a durable quiet preference. Observe real drafting, rereading and revision sessions. Measure unwanted interruptions and whether help resolved something; clicking alone is insufficient evidence.

2. **Make returning to a manuscript feel unusually good.** Remember the passage, unresolved question and relevant material the writer left with. A useful return might say: “This claim still needs an example; your earlier folio contains one.” I’d evolve the galley slip toward that continuity.

3. **Deepen the echoes into specific editorial connections.** The existing local matching is a sensible candidate finder. The exciting next step is explaining the relationship: an earlier example, a contradiction, a recurring image, a claim the writer has since refined. Every connection should open the exact supporting passage. [Current matching](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/flow-connections.ts:1)

4. **Make each intervention complete a small task.** A source should help substantiate a claim; a suggestion should support comparison, application and undo; an earlier passage should help resume an argument. I’d also persist unsent margin replies across reloads—the current contract preserves them only while the editor remains mounted.

5. **Consolidate before expanding the furniture.** Keep the House vocabulary, introduce it gradually, and extract candidate gathering, session lifecycle and placement from the large coordinator and surface components. Live model use and authenticated two-device sync also remain separate verification boundaries. [Verification](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/docs/flow-and-context.md:190)

My next milestone would be a real writing session where Twyne stays quiet during composition, offers one useful intervention, and makes returning tomorrow easier. That would establish the value of this direction more convincingly than another component.

settings.developer_instructions:
# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.
